title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problem_statement: Read one line of text and print the length of its longest contiguous substring in which every character appears at most once. Character comparisons are case-sensitive, and spaces count as characters. An empty line represents the empty string, whose answer is 0.
constraints: The input string contains between 0 and 100000 printable ASCII characters, inclusive.
The string may contain spaces and is case-sensitive.
The string contains no line-break characters.
input_format: Exactly one line containing the input string. The line may be empty; an empty line (a newline with no characters before it) represents the empty string. Spaces on the line are part of the string and must not be discarded.
output_format: Print one integer: the maximum length, measured in characters, of a contiguous substring with no repeated character. Print 0 for an empty string. Do not print extra text.

public_samples.explanation: The longest valid substrings include `abc`, `bca`, and `cab`, each of length 3.
Every character is the same, so any valid substring has length at most 1.
Uppercase `W` and lowercase `w` are different characters, so the whole string has no repeats.
The empty line represents an empty string, which has no characters.
The substring `b ca` has four distinct characters; the full string repeats `a`.

hints: A substring must be contiguous. Try thinking about a stretch of the string that contains no repeated characters.
As you scan from left to right, keep track of the start and end of a currently valid stretch. When a repeated character appears, the start may need to move forward.

A set can help detect characters in the current window, or a map can record each character's most recent index. Move the left boundary past an in-window repeat, and update the best length as you scan. Aim to process each character only a constant number of times.
common_beginner_mistakes: Searching for the longest subsequence rather than a substring; a substring must use adjacent positions.
Counting distinct characters in the whole string, even when their positions do not form one contiguous repeat-free segment.
Moving the window's left boundary backward when a repeated character was already outside the current window.
Moving the left boundary to the most recent duplicate's index instead of one position after it.
Resetting the whole window at every duplicate, which can miss a longer valid substring that begins inside the previous window.
Treating uppercase and lowercase letters as the same even though this mission defines comparisons as case-sensitive.
Removing spaces from input or not counting spaces as characters.
Using a nested search over all substrings, which can take quadratic time and is unsuitable for the maximum input length.
completion_criteria: Reads exactly one input line and preserves spaces; an empty line is accepted as the empty string.
Computes the length of the longest contiguous substring with all characters distinct.
Treats uppercase and lowercase characters as different and counts spaces as characters.
Handles empty input, repeated characters, and strings with no repeats.
Uses a sliding-window approach with a set or last-seen-index map to achieve O(n) expected time, rather than checking every substring.
Passes all public samples and separately maintained private tests.
